parameters.method: web verification of primary/secondary sources (see research/literature/SOURCES.md) + one computation: comparison of the CONVENTIONS.md ant with OEIS A261990 (python3 research/literature/check_oeis.py)

oeis_reconciliation.interpretation: OEIS A261990 has offset 0, so b(n) is the colour read at step n+1 in CONVENTIONS numbering. The OEIS comment 'begins repeating at the 9977th step' means b(n)==b(n+104) for n>=9977, i.e. the turn sequence is periodic from step 9978 onward, i.e. onset step s=9977 in CONVENTIONS.md (9977 steps completed before the periodic regime).

proven.claim: For every initial configuration the ant's trajectory is unbounded (Bunimovich-Troubetzkoy theorem, popularly 'Cohen-Kong theorem').
proven.source: L. A. Bunimovich, S. E. Troubetzkoy, J. Stat. Phys. 67 (1992) 289-302, doi:10.1007/BF01049035; attribution confirmed by Gale-Propp-Sutherland-Troubetzkoy 1995 and Gajardo-Moreira-Goles 2002
proven.level: VERIFIED (statement via refereed citations; primary paywalled)

proven.claim: The set of cells exited infinitely often has no corner cell.
proven.source: S. Troubetzkoy, Lewis-Parker lecture 'The ant', Alabama J. Math. 21(2) (1997) 3-15, as cited by Gajardo et al. 2002 and Etse 2026

proven.claim: Any boolean circuit can be evaluated by the trajectory of a single ant on a finite configuration; the cell-reachability problem is P-hard; with an infinite periodic configuration the ant is computationally universal and has undecidable problems.
proven.source: A. Gajardo, A. Moreira, E. Goles, Discrete Applied Mathematics 117 (2002) 41-50, doi:10.1016/S0166-218X(00)00334-6, arXiv:nlin/0306022

proven.claim: Generalized ants whose rule string has the even run-length property (e.g. LRRL, LLRR) exhibit recurrent bilateral symmetry.
proven.source: Gale, Propp, Sutherland, Troubetzkoy, Math. Intelligencer 17(3) (1995) 48-56, arXiv:math/9501233

proven.claim: On the triangular lattice the flipping-rotator ant propagates regardless of the initial configuration (average velocity 1/8).
proven.source: Grosfils, Boon, Cohen, Bunimovich, J. Stat. Phys. 97 (1999) 575-608, arXiv:cond-mat/9905168

proven.claim: Escape-time bounds on finite domains: n x n within (n+1)! steps; exact S(n,n) for n=1..9: 1,6,17,46,85,164,262,488,679.

open.claim: Highway conjecture: for every initial configuration with finite support the ant eventually builds the period-104 highway. OPEN as of all sources through June 2026.
sources: Lutfalla arXiv:2505.05426 (2025): 'little progress has been made towards proving or disproving this conjecture'
Etse arXiv:2606.26677 (2026): 'has never been formally established'
Wikipedia: 'no one has been able to prove that this is true for all such initial configurations'

open.claim: Decidability of problems whose input is a finite-support configuration (e.g. 'does the ant ever visit this cell?') is open; it would follow from the highway conjecture.

literature_figures.about 10,000: Gale et al. 1995; Gajardo et al. 2002; Wikipedia; Etse 2026 (rounded description)
literature_figures.9977: OEIS A261990 (2015), Tokarz arXiv:1807.08789 (2018): exact onset, 0-indexed = CONVENTIONS s
literature_figures.10647: MathWorld figure-caption step count, NOT an onset

attribution.introduced_by: Christopher G. Langton, 'Studying artificial life with cellular automata', Physica D 22 (1986) 120-149, doi:10.1016/0167-2789(86)90237-X; he called them 'vants'; paper contains no '10,000', no '104' and no 'highway'.
attribution.cohen_kong_name: from Ian Stewart, 'The Ultimate in Anty-Particles', Scientific American 271(1) (July 1994) 104-107; Wikipedia links Cohen to E. G. D. Cohen; Kong = X. P. Kong (inferred, not stated verbatim in any source read); MathWorld/Tokarz spell it 'Cohen-Kung'.

records.longest_transient_langton_ant_finite_con: none found in the literature; only the empty-grid 9977 is documented
records.other_rules: LLRRRL/LLRLRLL/LLLR etc. have published transients of 1e8 steps and more (Gajardo-Lutfalla-Rao 2025, Lutfalla 2025), not Langton's ant

notes: See research/literature/SOURCES.md for verbatim quotes, URLs and the VERIFIED/SECONDARY/UNVERIFIED label on each claim, and section 8 for misconceptions to avoid.
Only computed number: the OEIS reconciliation (check_oeis.py). Everything else is bibliographic.

Bunimovich-Troubetzkoy 1992, Gale 1993, Gale-Propp 1994, Stewart 1994 and Troubetzkoy 1997 are paywalled/unreachable from this sandbox; their contents are attested by the refereed papers that cite them.
